1 شَحُمَ , (S, Msb, K,) aor.
شَحُمَ , (K,) inf. n. شَحَامَةٌ, (MA, Msb,) He (a man, S, K) was, or became, fat; (S, MA, K;) as also شَحِمَ, aor.
شَحَمَ : (TA:) or he was, or became, abundant in the fat of his person. (Msb.) And شَحُمَتْ إِبِلُهُ (K) His camels were, or became, fat. (TA.) And شُحِمَتِ النَّاقَةُ; and شَحَمَت, aor.
شَحُمَ ; of the classes of عُنِىَ and نَصَرَ; inf. n. شَحْمٌ and شُحُومٌ; The she-camel became fat after leanness. (TA.) ―
-b2- شَحِمَ, (S, K,) aor.
شَحَمَ , (K,) inf. n. شَحَمٌ, (TA,) He was, or became, eagerly desirous of fat. (S, K, TA.) And He ate much fat. (TA.) ＝
-A2- شَحَمَهُ, (K,) or شَحَمَ أَصْحَابَهُ, (S,) aor.
شَحَمَ , (K,) inf. n. شَحْمٌ, (TA,) He fed him, or his companions, with fat; or gave him, or them, fat to eat. (S, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
